name: Pale Goldenrod
lede: Pale Goldenrod is the web color #EEE8AA, a pale, slightly greenish yellow named for a washed-out version of the goldenrod flower.

sections.title: The name
sections.body:
Paterson lists PaleGoldenrod as one of the 140 colors in the X11 color set, with the hex code #EEE8AA [1]. Oddly, his colour tables file it among the browns, although the swatch is a pale yellow [1]. The library also finds the swatch in the CSS list and in Ridgway's 1912 atlas, and ISCC-NBS block 104 names the nearest standard color "pale greenish yellow", only 1.3 units away [2].

It is a lightened [[goldenrod]]. Its nearest relatives are [[dark-goldenrod]], [[khaki]] and [[cream]], and it is far paler than the flower it is named for [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive of 23,781 paintings, 267 carry this color over at least five per cent of the canvas, as photographed, more often than 65 per cent of the named colors [3]. It peaks in the 1800s: 77 of 8,345 paintings, 1.7 times the usual rate [3]. In 68 per cent of the 145 paintings where we measured its rank, it plays a light [3]. The earliest dated match is a painting of about 1415, a floor not a first [3].
